steps: 1. Client intake, scope & file analyzability check
2. File preparation & CAT filter segmentation
3. TM leverage, termbase attachment & word-count matrix
4. Translation by native domain-qualified translator
5. Bilingual revision (Editing) by independent second linguist
6. Automated QA check (tags, numbers, terminology) + Final layout proofreading
7. Target file generation, PM sign-off, delivery & TM update
failure_points: Corrupted inline tags breaking target compilation
Skipped bilingual revision under rush deadline
Outdated reference TM overwriting approved terms
records.ai_automation_potential: 70–85% of initial drafting automated via LLM/NMT + MTQE routing; human revision shifts to high-risk/low-MTQE segments.

steps: 1. Developer commits UI code with externalized i18n keys (ICU MessageFormat)
2. CI webhook / Git connector pushes new/modified source keys to TMS
3. Automated screenshot/Figma context harvester attaches visual preview to keys
4. AI/MT pre-translation + Glossary check + MTQE triage
5. Human linguist reviews flagged keys in browser editor with visual context
6. Automated placeholder/ICU syntax linter validates target strings
7. TMS opens automated Git Pull Request or publishes OTA mobile bundle
failure_points: Hardcoded strings bypassed in source code
Concatenated strings destroying word order in SOV languages
records.ai_automation_potential: 85–95% of sync, pre-translation, context capture, and syntax validation automated.

records.workflow: Clinical Trial eCOA / PRO Linguistic Validation (ISPOR)
steps: 1. Concept elaboration guide created with instrument developer
2. Dual independent forward translations (T1 + T2) by native clinical linguists
3. Reconciliation into single harmonized target version (T12)
4. Blind back-translation (BT1 + BT2) into source language by native English translators
5. Back-translation review & harmonization with clinical survey developer
6. Cognitive debriefing interviews with 5–8 native patients in target country
7. Final clinical review, eCOA screen migration screenshot proofreading & certification
qa_gates: Patient comprehension threshold in cognitive debriefing
failure_points: Literal translation altering psychometric scale weight (e.g. 'mild' vs 'slight')
Back-translator having access to source text
Line wrap clipping clinical scale anchors on patient tablet
records.ai_automation_potential: 25–35% (AI assists with back-translation discrepancy comparison and schedule logistics, but regulatory bodies mandate human translators and real patient cognitive debriefing).

steps: 1. Source intake & automated content/risk classification (Tier 1 Legal/Brand vs. Tier 3 Support/UGC)
2. Context extraction agent pulls product metadata, UI screenshots, and user persona
3. RAG retrieval fetches top fuzzy TM matches, TBX glossary terms, and style rules
4. Dynamic model router selects optimal LLM/NMT per language pair & domain
5. Parallel candidate generation + Automated MQM/LLM-as-a-Judge Quality Estimation (QE)
6. Self-correction loop fixes deterministic tag/glossary violations; routes segments below QE threshold to human specialist
7. Human-in-the-loop expert sign-off -> automated delivery -> continuous feedback fine-tuning
failure_points: Uncalibrated QE model passing confident LLM hallucinations
Prompt injection in user-generated source content
Context window truncation dropping tail segments
records.ai_automation_potential: 80–95% autonomous execution for low/medium-risk tiers; 40–60% cycle-time reduction on high-risk human-reviewed tiers.
